rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who lose themselves destroy them through disbelief and stubborn resistance; they do not affirm the truth.
rows.anchor: أي أهلكوها بارتكاب الكفر والعناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What dwells in night and day includes everything that exists there and belongs to God; here dwelling means being located, not merely being at rest.
rows.anchor: أي وله كل متمكن ساكن

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: The verb means to inhabit a place, as when someone says that a person lives in a particular town.
rows.anchor: أنه من قولهم فلان يسكن بلد كذا أي يحله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The phrase means all creatures established in night and day.
rows.anchor: وهذا موافق لقول ابن عباس وله ما استقر في الليل والنهار من خلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes the phrase as what rests at night and moves by day to earn a living.
rows.anchor: ما سكن في الليل للاستراحة وتحرك في النهار للمعيشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This alternative mentions rest alone because it is more inclusive and common, movement ends in rest, and rest brings greater and broader relief.
rows.anchor: لأنه أعم وأكثر ولأن عاقبة التحرك السكون ولأن النعمة في السكون أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view includes both what rests and moves; Arabic may name one side and omit its counterpart, as in the reference to protection from heat, meaning heat and cold.
rows.anchor: قد تذكر أحد وجهي الشيء وتحذف الآخر لأن المذكور ينبه على المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning motion and rest points to the world's creation: every body undergoes these contingent states, so an agent must bring about motion or rest, both equally possible.
rows.anchor: كل جسم لا ينفك من الحوادث التي هي الحركة والسكون فإذا لا بد من محرك ومسكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is hearing because He is living without defect in a way that enables Him to hear sounds when they exist; this attribute applies eternally.
rows.anchor: السميع هو الذي على صفة يصح لأجلها أن يسمع المسموعات إذا وجدت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the governance of His creation and everything that can be known.
rows.anchor: العليم هو العالم بوجوده التدابير في خلقه وبكل ما يصح أن يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day stand for all things within them, since nothing is outside them; the concise expression is exceptionally eloquent.
rows.anchor: لأنه ليس يخرج منهما شيء فجمع كل الأشياء بهذا اللفظ القليل الحروف وهذا من أفصح ما يمكن

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: The poet depicts night as encompassing him, illustrating how night and day encompass all that exists within them.
rows.anchor: فإنك كالليل الذي هو مدركي وإن خلت إن المنتأى عنك واسع فجعل الليل مدركا له إذ كان مشتملا عليه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads fataḥnā with gemination throughout the Quran; Ibn ʿĀmir agrees except at the two cited door-opening passages, while Yaʿqūb lightens both in al-Qamar.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر فتحنا بالتشديد في جميع القرآن ووافقه ابن عامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read the form without gemination throughout, apart from positions to be discussed at their locations.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون في جميع ذلك بالتخفيف إلا مواضع قد اختلفوا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gemination conveys increase and emphasis, while the ungeminated form does not convey that intensification.
rows.anchor: من ثقل أراد التكثير والمبالغة ومن خفف لم يرد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-basāʾ means hardship or fear, and al-ḍarrāʾ means harm; al-basāʾ may also mean poverty.
rows.anchor: البأساء من البأس والخوف والضراء من الضر وقد يكون البأساء من البؤس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: They explain al-basāʾ and al-ḍarrāʾ here as poverty, misery, sickness, and pain.
rows.anchor: الفقر والبؤس والإسقام والأوجاع عن ابن عباس والحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadarruʿ means humble submission; the expression describes submitting to someone and asking him to give.
rows.anchor: والتضرع التذلل يقال ضرع فلان لفلان إذا بخع له وسأله أن يعطيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mublis means intensely regretful or despairing.
rows.anchor: والمبلس الشديد الحسرة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains mublis as someone whose argument has run out, citing Ruʾya's poetic use of iblās.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: المبلس المنقطع الحجة قال رؤية:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dābir describes the one who follows a people from behind and comes after them.
rows.anchor: دابر القوم الذي يدبرهم ويدبرهم لغتان وهو الذي يتلوهم من خلفهم

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says dābir means the root; cutting it means removing a people's foundations, as the cited poem illustrates.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: الدابر الأصل يقال قطع الله دابره أي أصله وأنشد:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another grammarian says dābir means the end of a matter.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره دابر الأمر آخره

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from ʿAbd Allāh uses dubariyyan for someone who reaches prayer only at the end of its time; hadith scholars pronounce it with a rounded initial vowel.
rows.anchor: وروي عن عبد الله أنه قال: من الناس من لا يأتي الصلاة ألا دبريا بضم الدال

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abū Zayd corrects the pronunciation to dubariyyan with fatḥa on both the dāl and bāʾ.
rows.anchor: قال أبو زيد: الصواب دبريا بفتح الدال والباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawlā is an exhortative particle used only with a verb; here it means why did they not humble themselves.
rows.anchor: لولا للتحضيض ولا يدخل إلا على الفعل ومعناه هلا تضرعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that their hearts hardened is linked to the implied meaning of the preceding question, which indicates that they did not humble themselves.
rows.anchor: معطوف على تأويل الكلام الأول فإن في قوله { هلا تضرعوا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghtatan is a verbal noun used adverbially to mean that they were seized by surprise.
rows.anchor: مصدر وقع موقع الحال أي أخذناهم مباغتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells the Prophet about earlier nations who opposed their messengers, warning that opponents of this Messenger face the same fate; the word messengers is omitted concisely but understood.
rows.anchor: وها هنا محذوف وتقديره رسلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle laʿalla expresses the worshipers' hope that the afflicted people might humble themselves, not uncertainty in God.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: لعل ترج وهذا الترجي للعباد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the phrase as affliction intended to make people humble, as in the account of Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: المعنى فأخذناهم بذلك ليكون ما يرجوه العباد منهم من التضرع كما قال في قصة فرعون

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh says the command to Moses and Aaron expresses their hope, although God knows what will follow.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه: المعنى اذهبا أنتما على رجائكما فالله عالم بما يكون من وراء ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The peoples were so hardened that even hardship to themselves and their wealth did not make them submit; this account consoles the Prophet.
rows.anchor: بلغوا من القسوة إلى أن أخذوا بالشدة في أنفسهم وأموالهم ليخضعوا ويذلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When punishment came, they did not humble themselves but persisted in disbelief, unaffected by admonition.
rows.anchor: فأقاموا على كفرهم فلم تنجح فيهم العظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan beautified their deeds through whispering and enticement to sin for its immediate pleasure.
rows.anchor: بالوسوسة والإغراء بالمعصية لما فيها من عاجل اللذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses refute those who say God did not will faith for unbelievers: He says He afflicted them so they would humble themselves and says Satan beautified their disbelief, contrary to the Mujabbira's claim that God did so.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا حجة على من قال إن الله لم يرد من الكافرين الإيمان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Forgetting the warning means abandoning the admonition and, more precisely, ceasing to act on it.
rows.anchor: أي تركوا ما وعظوا به عن ابن عباس وتأويله تركوا العمل بذلك

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says they abandoned what the messengers had called them to.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تركوا ما دعاهم إليه الرسل عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The opened doors of everything are every blessing and bounty from heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: أي كل نعمة وبركة من السماء والأرض عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil takes the phrase as all kinds of good that had previously been closed to them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أبواب كل شيء كان مغلقا عنهم من الخير عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God first tested them with hardship to prompt supplication and repentance, then opened blessings and expanded provision so they would desire the afterlife.
rows.anchor: فلما تركوا ذلك فتح عليهم أبواب النعم والتوسعة في الرزق ليرغبوا بذلك في نعيم الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prosperity could invite obedience through gentleness instead of severity, or make punishment harsher by moving them from luxury to painful torment.
rows.anchor: ليدعوهم ذلك إلى الطاعة فإن الدعاء إلى الطاعة يكون تارة بالعنف وتارة باللطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They rejoiced in their gifts and indulged in them without recognizing them as God's blessing or responding with gratitude.
rows.anchor: واشتغلوا بالتلذذ وأظهروا السرور بما أعطوه ولم يروه نعمة من الله تعالى حتى يشكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being seized means that punishment descended upon them suddenly, when they were unaware.
rows.anchor: أي مفاجأة من حيث لا يشعرون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Iblās here means despairing of rescue and mercy.
rows.anchor: أي آيسون من النجاة والرحمة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: البلخي
rows.claim: Al-Balkhī interprets the people as humbled and submissive.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أذلة خاضعون عن البلخي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that they were bewildered and had no argument; these meanings are close.
rows.anchor: وقيل: متحيرون منقطعوا الحجة، والمعاني متقاربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All things in the phrase means abundance and emphasis, not literally every item, as in the Queen of Sheba's statement that she was given everything.
rows.anchor: التكثير والتفخيم دون التعميم وهو مثل قوله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that when God gives people more despite their sins, that bounty is a form of gradual entrapment; the Prophet then recited this verse.
rows.anchor: إذا رأيت الله تعالى يعطي على المعاصي فإن ذلك استدراج منه

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī warns that someone who sees his Lord continually bestow blessings should be wary.
rows.anchor: يا ابن آدم إذا رأيت ربك يتابع عليك نعمه فاحذره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cutting the dābir means utterly destroying the wrongdoers so no descendant or offspring remains.
rows.anchor: فاستؤصل الذين ظلموا بالعذاب فلم يبق لهم عقب ولا نسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God praises Himself for destroying His enemies and exalting His messengers after sending, warning, delaying, and testing the people through hardship and prosperity; He is praised in every circumstance.
rows.anchor: أرسل إليهم وأنظرهم بعد كفرهم وأخذهم بالبأساء والضراء واختبرهم بالمحنة والبلاء ثم بالنعمة والرخاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse teaches believers to praise God for protecting them from wrongdoers and shows that their destruction is a blessing deserving praise.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا تعليم للمؤمنين ليحمدوا الله تعالى على كفايته إياهم شر الظالمين

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh defines piety as avoiding God's prohibitions and doubtful matters, since carelessness about doubtful matters can lead unknowingly to the forbidden.
rows.anchor: الورع هو الذي يتورع عن محارم الله ويجتنب هؤلاء وإذا لم يتق الشبهات وقع في الحرام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Someone able to condemn wrongdoing who does not do so loves that God be disobeyed; loving the survival of wrongdoers likewise loves disobedience and hostility to God.
rows.anchor: وإذا رأى المنكر ولم ينكره وهو يقدر عليه فقد أحب أن يعصى الله

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh links God's praise for destroying wrongdoers to this verse.
rows.anchor: وأن الله حمد نفسه على إهلاك الظالمين فقال فقطع دابر القوم الذين ظلموا

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza alone reads istahwā with an alif and imāla; the other readers use the feminine tāʾ form istahwat.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة وحده استهويه بألف ممالة والباقون استهوته بالتاء المعجمة من فوق

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says both reading forms are sound, with poetic usage supporting the variant forms.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي كلا المذهبين حسن قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istahwā derives from hawā, falling from a height, and describes one who strays from the straight path; zalla likewise shifts from a spatial slip to a mistake in conduct.
rows.anchor: استهواه من قولهم هوى من حالق إذا تردى منه ويشبه به الذي زل عن الطريق المستقيم

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: A poem uses zalla for a literal slip on a slippery place, supporting the metaphorical extension to error.
rows.anchor: قام على منزعة زلخ فزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahwā and istahwā have the same sense, just as azalla and istazalla, and ajāba and istajāba do.
rows.anchor: فكذلك هوى وأهواه غيره فيقال أهويته واستهويته بمعنى

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: The cited line uses istajāba in the sense of ajāba.
rows.anchor:
قال:
فلم يستجبه عند ذاك مجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥayrān means a person perplexed in a matter and unable to find a way out; the verb is ḥāra and the plural is ḥiyārā.
rows.anchor: والحيران المتردد في أمر لا يهتدي إلى المخرج منه والفعل منه حار يحار حيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison is an accusative description of an omitted verbal noun, meaning an invocation like that of someone whom devils have led astray; ḥayrān is a circumstantial accusative, and the clauses describe him and his companions.
rows.anchor: كالذي استهوته في موضع نصب صفة لمصدر محذوف تقديره أندعو من دون الله دعاء مثل دعاء الذي استهوته الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic permits amarnā li-nuslima as well as constructions with an and bāʾ; the lām expresses purpose, as in a poet's statement meaning I wish to forget.
rows.anchor: ومن قال أمرتك لتفعل المعنى أمرتك للفعل وقال الزجاج: التقدير أمرنا كي نسلم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses the command as meaning that the believers were ordered in order to submit.
rows.anchor: أريد لأنسى ذكرها فكأنما تمثل لي ليلى بكل سبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet, the human addressee, or any listener is commanded to address idol-worshiping unbelievers about worshipping what can neither benefit them if worshipped nor harm them if left.
rows.anchor: يا محمد لهؤلاء الكفار الذين يدعون إلى عبادة الأصنام أو قل أيها الإنسان أو أيها السامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being turned back on one's heels is an idiom for failing to attain one's aim and retreating; here it means abandoning the best religion after God guided them.
rows.anchor: هذا مثل يقولون لكل خائب لم يظفر بحاجته رد على عقبيه ونكص على عقبيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the devils who lure the person as ghūls calling people to follow desire in wildernesses.
rows.anchor: معناه استغوته الغيلان في المهامه عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say the devils call him to follow desire, destroy him, carry him away, or lead him astray; the last is attributed to Abū Muslim and being carried away to Niftawayh.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه دعته الشياطين إلى اتباع الهوى. وقيل: أهلكته. وقيل: ذهبت به عن نفطويه.

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim explains the phrase as meaning that the devils led the person astray.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أضلته عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companions call the bewildered person to the clear path, but he neither accepts nor comes because Satan has overtaken him and he wanders without guidance.
rows.anchor: يقولون له أئتنا ولا يقبل منهم ولا يصير إليهم لأنه قد تحير لاستيلاء الشيطان عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's guidance is His direction to monotheism and religion, leading to soundness and right guidance; it must be followed rather than the polytheists' invitation.
rows.anchor: أي دلالة الله لنا على توحيده وأمر دينه هو الهدى الذي يؤدي المستدل به إلى الصلاح والرشاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means either to submit to the Lord of the worlds or to entrust one's affairs to Him and rely on Him.
rows.anchor: وأمرنا أن نسلم. وقيل: معناه أن نسلم أمورنا ونفوضها إلى الله

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وورش
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Warsh through al-Bukhārī's route read raʾā kawkaban with fatḥa on rāʾ and kasra on hamza wherever it occurs.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وورش من طريق البخاري رأى كوكبا بفتح الراء وكسر الهمزة حيث كان

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وخلف ويحيى عن أبي بكر
rows.claim: These readers pronounce both rāʾ and hamza with kasra in raʾā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وخلف ويحيى عن أبي بكر رأى بكسر الراء والهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers use fatḥa on both letters; Abū ʿAlī's detailed argument for the readings was omitted to avoid length.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بفتح الراء والهمزة. الحجة: ذكر أبو علي الوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Janna, janna-hu, and ajanna describe night darkening until it conceals things; the root also explains why jinn are named for being hidden from sight.
rows.anchor: جن عليه الليل وجنه الليل وأجنه الليل إذا أظلم حتى يستر بظلمته

rows.speaker: الهذلي
rows.claim: The Hudhalī poet uses jannah for water covered by the dark shade before dawn.
rows.anchor: وماء وردت قبيل الكرى وقد جنه السدف الأدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajanantu and jannantu mean that one buried a dead person in a grave.
rows.anchor: ويقال أجننت الميت وجننته إذا واريته في اللحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afala means to set or disappear.
rows.anchor: وأفل يأفل أفوالا إذا غاب

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhū al-Rumma's poem uses the word āfilāt for setting stars.
rows.anchor:
قال ذو الرمة:
مصابيح ليست باللواتي يقودها نجوم ولا بالآفلات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buzūgh means rising; the crescent is called hilāl during the month's first three nights and then qamar for the rest of the month, a name associated with its whiteness.
rows.anchor: والبزوغ الطلوع يقال بزغت الشمس إذا طلعت ويسمى ثلاث ليال من أول الشهر الهلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective aqmar means white, as in a white camel.
rows.anchor: وإنما يسمى قمرا لبياضه وحمار أقمر أبيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥanīf is one inclined toward the truth.
rows.anchor: والحنيف المائل إلى الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine demonstrative this is understood as this rising light, so the noun and predicate are masculine, parallel to the feminine sun-rising construction.
rows.anchor: إن التقدير هذا النور الطالع ربي ليكون الخبر والمخبر عنه جميعا على التذكير

rows.speaker: ابن فضال المجاشعي
rows.claim: Ibn Faḍḍāl says God narrates that the sun is rising, while Abraham's phrase this is my Lord is in his own speech; non-Arabic may treat sun as masculine, and God conveys Abraham's language.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن فضال المجاشعي قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says the sun is feminine as an honorific because of its greater light, like words such as nissāba and ʿallāma; the moon is less bright.
rows.anchor: تأنيثها تفخيم لها لكثرة ضيائها على حد قولهم نسابة وعلامة وليس القمر كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-shams takes the definite article despite being singular because the name can denote sunlight or the sun's body, ray, genus, or an individual; personal names such as Zayd do not.
rows.anchor: لأن شعاع الشمس يقع عليه اسم الشمس فاحتيج إلى التعريف إذا قصد إلى جرم الشمس أو إلى الشعاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the signs shown to Abraham, God explains how Abraham inferred the truth from them.
rows.anchor: لما تقدم ذكر الآيات التي أراها الله تعالى إبراهيم ع بين سبحانه كيف استدل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The star Abraham saw is variously identified as Venus or Jupiter.
rows.anchor: واختلف في الكوكب الذي رآه فقيل هو الزهرة. وقيل: هو المشتري

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم البلخي
rows.claim: Al-Balkhī and others say Abraham spoke during mature rational reflection: impressed by a star worshipped by his people, he entertained it as Lord hypothetically, then its setting showed it was created; he reasoned similarly from the moon and sun and turned to their Creator.
rows.anchor: وهذا اختيار أبي القاسم البلخي وغيره

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم البلخي
rows.claim: The interval for rational reflection lasts more than an hour and less than a month, though only God knows its exact duration.
rows.anchor: وزمان مهلة النظر هي أكثر من ساعة وأقل من شهر ولا يعلم ما بينهما إلا الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī's second view has Abraham say this before puberty, while nearing maturity; he initially supposes the luminous bodies might be his Lord, then recognizes their changing and asks God for guidance.
rows.anchor: وثانيها: أنه إنما قال ذلك قبل بلوغه ولما قارب كمال العقل حركته الخواطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the moon rises, its size, brilliance, and spreading light prompt Abraham's provisional statement; its setting shows that it cannot be divine, so he asks God to guide him lest he join those astray.
rows.anchor: وعلم أنه لا يجوز أن يكون ذلك صفة الإله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun appears greater than the star and moon; after it sets Abraham rejects the people's idols and, once his reasoning matures, turns wholly to the Creator as the maker of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: قال هذا ربي هذا أكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning his face means turning himself toward the Creator, sincerely inclined away from associationism and toward pure devotion.
rows.anchor: أي مخلصا مائلا عن الشرك إلى الإخلاص

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī prefers the second account, in which Abraham reaches full reason and concludes that bodies need an originator before declaring his faith to his people.
rows.anchor: وهذا اختيار أبي علي الجبائي ويسأل عن القول الأول كيف قال ع هذا ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first view need not make Abraham falsely claim knowledge: he may have posed the claim hypothetically, as one supposes a body's eternity to expose the absurdity of that assumption.
rows.anchor: أنه لم يقل ذلك مخبرا وإنما قاله فارضا ومقدرا على سبيل التأمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he reported a thought he could provisionally entertain during inquiry and then abandon when evidence refuted it.
rows.anchor: أخبر عن ظنة قد يجوز أن يظن المتفكر في حال فكره ونظره ما لا أصل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Abraham's mother gave birth in a cave to hide him from Nimrod, so he may not have seen the sky before leaving it; alternatively, he may have seen it without yet reflecting on its signs because reflection was not yet obligatory.
rows.anchor: قد روي أنه أمه كانت ولدته في مغارة خوفا من أن يقتله نمرود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view says Abraham knew with certainty that God could not have the properties of stars; he used this is my Lord to challenge idolaters, either attributing the claim to their beliefs or asking a question with the interrogative hamza omitted.
rows.anchor: أن إبراهيم ع لم يقل هذا ربي على طريق الشك بل كان عالما موقنا أن ربه سبحانه لا يجوز أن يكون بصفة الكواكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic often omits an interrogative hamza, as shown by the cited lines of Aws ibn Ḥajar, al-Akhṭal, ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa, and an unnamed poet.
rows.anchor: وإما على أن يكون قال ذلك مستفهما وأسقط حرف الاستفهام للاستغناء عنه وقد كثر مجيء ذلك في كلام العرب

rows.speaker: أوس بن حجر
rows.claim: Aws ibn Ḥajar's line is cited as an example of dropping the interrogative hamza.
rows.anchor:
قال أوس بن حجر:
لعمرك لا أدري وإن كنت داريا شعيب بن شهم أم شعيب بن منقر

rows.speaker: الأخطل
rows.claim: Al-Akhṭal's line is another example of an omitted interrogative hamza.
rows.anchor:
وقال الأخطل:
كذبتك عينك أم رأيت بواسط غلس الظلام من الرباب خيالا

rows.speaker: عمر بن أبي ربيعة
rows.claim: ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa's line means did you love her, illustrating the omitted hamza.
rows.anchor:
وقال عمر بن أبي ربيعة:
ثم قالوا تحبها قلت بهرا

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line similarly means are they them, with the question hamza omitted.
rows.anchor:
وقال آخر:
رفوني وقالوا يا خويلد لا ترع فقلت وأنكرت الوجوه هم هم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the phrase in 90:11 as a question meaning did he not scale the obstacle, with the hamza omitted.
rows.anchor: معناه أفلا اقتحم فحذف حرف الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth view says Abraham feigned the claim to expose his people's poor reasoning and the error of worshipping created things subject to changing states; he meant this is my Lord according to your claim.
rows.anchor: أنه ع إنما قال استخداعا للقوم يريهم قصور علمهم وبطلان عبادتهم لمخلوق جار عليه أعراض الحوادث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation supplies an unspoken condition: if the stone you claim is lord were truly so, then the star, moon, and sun would be my lords, though none is actually a lord.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه نوى في قلبه الشرط أي إن كان ربكم هذا الحجر كما تزعمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage proves bodies are originated: their setting makes their motion especially clear and hard to dispute, and motion and rest cannot belong to an eternal God.
rows.anchor: وإنما استدل إبراهيم بالأفول على حدوثها لأن حركتها بالأفول أظهر ومن الشبهة أبعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If bodies move and rest, they are created and require a maker; making them requires power, their ordered design requires knowledge, and a being with power and knowledge must be living and existent.
rows.anchor: وإذا جازت عليها الحركة والسكون فلا بد أن تكون مخلوقة محدثة وإذا كانت محدثة فلا بد لها من محدث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account warns Arab polytheists against idol worship and urges them to follow Abraham's reflective search for truth, since they revere their ancestors and acknowledge Abraham's virtue.
rows.anchor: تنبيه لمشركي العرب وزجر لهم عن عبادة الأصنام وحث لهم على سلوك طريق أبيهم إبراهيم

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير والتاريخ
rows.claim: Exegetes and historians place Abraham's birth under Nimrod ibn Canaan; some call Nimrod a governor under Kaykaus, while others say he was an independent king.
rows.anchor: ذكر أهل التفسير والتاريخ أن إبراهيم ع ولد في زمن نمرود بن كنعان وزعم بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say astrologers predicted a child would destroy Nimrod and his kingdom; others say the warning came from prophetic books, and al-Suddī reports Nimrod dreamed a star extinguished the sun and moon and was told a boy would end his rule.
rows.anchor: رأى نمرود كأن كوكبا طلع فذهب بضوء الشمس والقمر فسأل عنه فعبر بأنه يولد غلام يذهب ملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod ordered male infants killed, men separated from women, and pregnant women detained until delivery so newborn boys could be killed and girls released.
rows.anchor: أمر بقتل كل ولد يولد تلك السنة وأمر بأن يعزل الرجال عن النساء وبأن يتفحص عن أحوال النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Abraham's mother was near delivery she fled, gave birth in a cave, wrapped him, blocked its entrance with a stone, and left; God fed him milk from his thumb and made him grow extraordinarily fast.
rows.anchor: خرجت أمه هاربة فذهبت به إلى غار ولفته في خرقة ثم جعلت على باب الغار صخرة

rows.speaker: أبو روق ومحمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Rawq and Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq report that his mother visited and he sucked four fingers, receiving water, milk, honey, dates, and clarified butter from them.
rows.anchor: عن أبي روق ومحمد بن إسحاق ولما خرج من السرب نظر إلى النجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After leaving the cave near the month's end, Abraham saw a star, then the moon and sun, and spoke as described; after seeing his people worship idols he opposed and denounced them, leading to debates.
rows.anchor: ولما خرج من السرب نظر إلى النجم وكان آخر الشهر فرأى الكوكب قبل القمر ثم رأى الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kufans and Yaʿqūb read darajāt without nunation; the other readers use the construct phrase darajāt man nashāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة ويعقوب درجات منونا والباقون درجات من نشاء بالإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufan readers other than ʿĀṣim, and al-Laysʿ, geminate and open the lām in al-Laysʿ here and in Ṣād; the other readers use a silent lām and open yāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم والليسع بتشديد اللام وفتحها وسكون الياء ههنا وفي ص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the construct reading, the raised things are degrees granted to whomever God wills; with nunation, the person who possesses degrees is raised.
rows.anchor: من أضاف درجات ذهب إلى أن المرفوعة هي الدرجات لمن يشاء ومن نون ذهب إلى أن المرفوع صاحب الدرجات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construct reading is supported by 2:253: whoever is favored over another has had his rank raised above that person.
rows.anchor: ويقوي قراءة من أضاف قوله تلك الرسل فضلنا بعضهم على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nunated reading is supported by 2:253, which speaks of some messengers being raised in degrees.
rows.anchor: ويدل على قراءة من نون قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The degrees in 43:32 concern worldly rank and changing circumstances, as the context is about the division of worldly livelihoods.
rows.anchor: فإنه في الرتب وارتفاع الأحوال في الدنيا واتضاعها لأن قبله نحن قسمنا بينهم معيشتهم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the lām in the geminated reading al-Laysʿ is an extra letter, then distinguishes a definite article that identifies a known referent from one added as a prefix.
rows.anchor: وأما من قرأ الليسع باللام فإن هذه اللام زائدة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The first definite article can refer to a mutually known person; another can refer to a generic concept known intellectually rather than through the senses.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى معهود بينك وبين المخاطب نحو الرجل إذا أردت به رجلا عرفتماه بعهد

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: In this man and in vocative O man, the article points to someone present to be seen rather than to a previously agreed referent.
rows.anchor: وأما نحو مررت بهذا الرجل فإنما أشير به إلى الشاهد الحاضر

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl treats names such as al-ʿAbbās, al-Ḥārith, and al-Ḥasan as if the article made them the very quality or thing itself; without that construction Arabic also has Ḥārith and ʿAbbās without the article.
rows.anchor: فأما نحو العباس والحارث والحسن فإنما دخلت الألف واللام فيها على تنزيل أنها صفات
